newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures came under pressure late on Tuesday after hitting a new high but traders said the contract would probably cling onto its recent gains ahead of key German economic data due this week.

The March bond future broke through its previous high of 132.50 early in the session and surged to 132.94 when the U.S. market opened then a reversal of the U.S. gains prevented the contract reaching the psychologically important 133 level.
Ten-year bond yields fell to new lows on the back of the futures rally. The 6.50 percent 2006 OAT yield touched 5.27 percent while the 5.50 percent 2007 OAT yield fell to 5.35.

One trader said the market remained bullish and that the contract would probably stay around 132.60 ahead of the publication of the key German Ifo business climate survey and a U.S. January consumer prices report later this week.
Futures traders said earlier hopes that the Ifo survey would be weaker than expected had given the market its early boost and strength in the Bund market had supported the rally.
Traders said the five-year part of the curve suffered slightly after the Treasury announced it would be selling 22 to 24 billion francs of the new 4.75 percent 2002 BTAN on Thursday.
